**On load:** `AppProvider` (`src/app/provider.tsx`) wraps the whole app in `AuthLoader`, which comes from `configureAuth` in `src/lib/auth.tsx`. While it loads, a spinner is shown. `AuthLoader` calls `getUser`, which does `api.get('/auth/me')`, and stores the result as the `useUser` query. The `api` client is an Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts` with `withCredentials: true`, so the session cookie is sent. `ProtectedRoute` (also in `src/lib/auth.tsx`) wraps the protected routes in `src/app/router.tsx`. If `user.data` is empty, it redirects to `paths.auth.login.getHref(location.pathname)`.

**On a 401:** the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` handles it. It first adds an error toast with the server's message (or the Axios error message), for every failed request. Then, if `error.response.status === 401`, it sets `window.location.href` to the login path with a `redirectTo` value, and rejects the promise so the caller still sees the error.

One thing to check: the `redirectTo` logic is broken. It creates `new URLSearchParams()` (empty) and reads `redirectTo` from that, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. The query string of the current page is dropped, and the intended "come back to the page I wanted" behaviour only partly works. The code is `src/lib/api-client.ts:34-36`; the fix would read `window.location.search` instead.

Also, `/auth/me` goes through the same interceptor. A visitor who is not signed in will likely see an error toast and be redirected by the interceptor during the initial load, not by `ProtectedRoute`. I read the code but did not run the app to confirm that sequence.

No files were changed.
